answers.explanation: The shell ships with the OS and runs outside the kernel.
It solves a user's problem and has nothing to do with running the system.
Allocating the CPU is core OS work, so it's in the kernel.
Users can be people, machines, or other computers.
An I/O device, one of the basic computing resources.
Preventing errors and improper use is the control program's job.
Resolving conflicting requests for resources is the allocator's job.
That's what "the one program running at all times" means.
